title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: §2 of a manuscript on algebraic cycles. Here A^i_alg(X) denotes cycles of codimension i algebraically equivalent to 0 modulo rational equivalence, i.e. the algebraically trivial part of the Chow group. The previous page (Def. 2.5) defined an 'algebraic map' φ: Y(k) → A^i_alg(X). The condition is that φ factors through the Albanese A_Y, and that some multiple Nφ is induced by a cycle on X × A_Y.

This page does three things.
(1) N.B. Fix a base point y_0 ∈ Y. The group of algebraic families Y(k) → A^i_alg(X) splits as A^i_alg(X) × Hom_alg(A_Y, A^i_alg(X)). The first factor is the value at y_0. The second factor consists of the families that are group homomorphisms, i.e. vanish at the origin. This is the usual 'constant plus homomorphism' decomposition, coming from the Albanese universal property and rigidity. So one may restrict to algebraic homomorphisms A(k) → A^i_alg(X) with A an abelian variety.
(2) An abelian variety A is identified with its own group of 0-cycles algebraically equivalent to 0: A(k) ≅ A_{0,alg}(A) = A^α_alg(A) with α = dim A, via the Albanese map. Writing P^i(X) for A^i_alg(X), the special case becomes a homomorphism P^α(A) → P^i(X). This is a particular case of a general notion of algebraic homomorphism φ: P^j(X') → P^i(X).
(3) Definition: a group homomorphism φ: P^j(X') → P^i(X) is 'algebraic' if some Nφ (N > 0) is induced by an algebraic cycle (correspondence) on X × X'. Such φ is then 'defined by a correspondence with rational coefficients' Z/N. Caveat: an arbitrary Q-correspondence does not define a homomorphism of the integral groups P^j(X') → P^i(X). Division by N is ill-defined because of torsion in these divisible groups, so some compatibility condition is needed. The last line likely begins the statement that such homomorphisms compose.

The purpose is to set up a category whose objects are the groups P^i(X) and whose morphisms are 'algebraic homomorphisms'. This is a motivic/correspondence-theoretic framework for comparing Chow groups with abelian varieties: algebraic representatives, intermediate Jacobians. The next page uses it to formulate a transposition duality between P^i(X) and P^j(X) for i + j = n + 1.
errors: The rational-coefficient remark is incomplete. Z/N acting on the integral group is ambiguous because A^i_alg(X) is divisible but has torsion (Roitman/Bloch phenomena). φ is determined by Nφ only up to N-torsion-valued maps. The remark is correct in spirit but no precise criterion is given.
Implicit assumption: A_Y and the Albanese parametrization are used without saying that the algebraic map determines the homomorphism uniquely. This is fine by rigidity over an algebraically closed k.

ideas.what: Algebraic maps from a pointed variety into A^i_alg(X) decompose as a constant plus an algebraic homomorphism from the Albanese
ideas.modern_name: Albanese universal property / rigidity for maps into Chow groups

ideas.what: Identification of an abelian variety A with its group of algebraically-trivial 0-cycles A_0,alg(A)
ideas.modern_name: Albanese isomorphism A ≅ CH_0(A)_alg / Albanese kernel

ideas.what: Definition of 'algebraic homomorphism' P^j(X') → P^i(X) between groups of algebraically-trivial cycles: some multiple N·φ is induced by a correspondence on X × X'
ideas.modern_name: homomorphisms induced by correspondences, up to isogeny; relates to Samuel's regular homomorphisms and Murre's algebraic representatives

ideas.what: Warning that a Q-correspondence need not induce a homomorphism on the integral Chow groups (torsion/divisibility issue)
ideas.modern_name: integral vs rational Chow motives; torsion in CH^i_alg

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a category of groups P^i(X) (algebraically trivial cycles) with 'algebraic homomorphisms' (correspondences up to multiplication by N). This is meant to include abelian varieties via A ≅ P^dim A(A), and leads into a transposition duality P^i ↔ P^{n+1-i} on the next page. This is close to, and anticipates, the modern study of algebraic representatives and their duality (Murre; Achter–Casalaina-Martin–Vial). However, the notion itself is fairly natural and essentially Samuel's.
missed.quote: Un homom. de groupes φ est dit "algébrique" s'il existe un entier N>0 tel que Nφ soit définissable par un cycle algébrique sur X × X'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This shows Grothendieck around 1965–71 treating abelian varieties as a full subcategory of a cycle-theoretic category of 'P^i' groups. That is an early isogeny-category formulation of algebraic representatives, mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean but natural foundational definitions (algebraic homomorphisms between Chow groups of algebraically trivial cycles, induced by correspondences up to N). They largely parallel Samuel's regular homomorphisms and later Murre. Their interest is historical, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Subscript is 'alg' (A^i_alg(X)), not 'alb' as on the previous page's transcription.
The margin formula reads 'A(k) ≃ P^α(A) → P^i(X)'.
Last line likely reads 'Ces homom. se composent' (these homomorphisms compose), not 'Un homom. de composantes'.
The parenthetical near the end may read '(= si leurs degrés sont les bons ....)' rather than 'dénominateurs sont bornés'; the reading is uncertain.
